sql.sqlStatement: Clear the 'data' worksheet
RESET
Specify the workbook containing the data
SET DATA FILE
Log errors to a file
ENABLE LOGGING
Give the graph a title

SELECT 'graph'                                                              AS [Item], 
       CStr(MIN([StartYear])) & ' - ' & CStr(MAX([StartYear])) & ' Roadmap' AS [Label], 
       'Page Title'                                                         AS [Style Name] 
FROM   [timeline$]
Creates a chain of edges from year to year. We use ENUMERATE syntax to fill in any potential years which may not have any events in them.

SELECT TRUE AS [ENUMERATE], MIN(CLng([StartYear])) AS [START AT], MAX(CLng([EndYear])) AS [STOP AT], 1 AS [STEP BY], 
       '{step}' AS [Item], 'Transparent Edge' AS [Style Name],
       TRUE AS [CREATE EDGES]
FROM   [timeline$]
WHERE  IsNumeric([StartYear])
Add styling to all the year nodes created in the chain above

SELECT TRUE AS [ENUMERATE], MIN(CLng([StartYear])) AS [START AT], MAX(CLng([EndYear])) AS [STOP AT], 1 AS [STEP BY], 
       '{step}' AS [Item], 
       '{step}' AS [Label], 
       'Year'   AS [Style Name]
FROM   [timeline$]
WHERE  IsNumeric([StartYear])
Create the edges between the start and finish of an event which spans multiple quarters

SELECT [EventID] & '_Start'                  AS [Item], 
       [EventID] & '_End'                    AS [Related Item],
       [EventID] & ' - ' & [EventName]       AS [Label] , 
       [Status]                              AS [Style Name], 
       20                                    AS [SPLIT LENGTH]
FROM   [timeline$]
WHERE  [StartYear] IS NOT NULL 
AND    [EndYear]   IS NOT NULL
AND    [StartYear] & [StartQuarter] <> [EndYear] & [EndQuarter]
ORDER BY [StartYear]    DESC, 
         [StartQuarter] DESC
Create the edges between events that start and finish in the same year and quarter

SELECT [EventID] & '_Start'            AS [Item], 
       [EventID] & '_Start'            AS [Related Item],
       [EventID] & ' - ' & [EventName] AS [Label] , 
       [Status]                        AS [Style Name], 
       20                              AS [SPLIT LENGTH]
FROM   [timeline$]
WHERE  [StartYear] IS NOT NULL 
AND    [EndYear]   IS NOT NULL
AND    [StartYear] & [StartQuarter] = [EndYear] & [EndQuarter]
ORDER BY [StartYear]    ASC, 
         [StartQuarter] ASC
Create the edges that highlight any Event dependencies

SELECT 
    'dependency' AS [Label],
    SWITCH(
        t.[StartYear] & t.[StartQuarter] = t.[EndYear] & t.[EndQuarter],
            d.[Must Complete] & '_Start',
        True,
            d.[Must Complete] & '_End'
    ) AS [Item],
    d.[Before the Start Of] & '_Start' AS [Related Item],
    'Dependency' AS [Style Name]
FROM 
    [dependencies$]        AS d
    INNER JOIN [timeline$] AS t
        ON t.[EventID] = d.[Must Complete]
WHERE
    d.[Must Complete]       IS NOT NULL
AND d.[Before the Start Of] IS NOT NULL;

Place all the events of a given year on the same rank by placing the nodes in subgroups with CREATE RANK. 
We use ITERATE to create a subgroup per year, as a normal query would put the results into one giant subgroup.
Nodes must be grouped before the styling is applied. 
NOTE: 2 single quotes are required on each side of text (e.g. ''same'') as it is a string within a string (the whole SQL).

SELECT TRUE AS [ITERATE],
  'SELECT DISTINCT [StartYear] AS [ID] FROM [timeline$]' 
  AS [SQL FOR ID],

  'SELECT TRUE AS [CREATE RANK], ''same'' AS [RANK], [StartYear]            AS [ITEM] FROM [timeline$] 
   WHERE [StartYear] = {ID} AND [StartYear] & [StartQuarter] <> [EndYear] & [EndQuarter]
      UNION
   SELECT TRUE AS [CREATE RANK], ''same'' AS [RANK], [EventID] & ''_Start'' AS [ITEM] FROM [timeline$] 
   WHERE [StartYear] = {ID} AND [StartYear] & [StartQuarter] <> [EndYear] & [EndQuarter]
      UNION
   SELECT TRUE AS [CREATE RANK], ''same'' AS [RANK], [EventID] & ''_Start''  AS [ITEM] FROM [timeline$] 
   WHERE [StartYear] = {ID} AND [StartYear] & [StartQuarter] = [EndYear] & [EndQuarter]
      UNION
   SELECT TRUE AS [CREATE RANK], ''same'' AS [RANK], [EndYear]              AS [ITEM] FROM [timeline$] 
   WHERE [EndYear]   = {ID} AND [StartYear] & [StartQuarter] <> [EndYear] & [EndQuarter]
      UNION
   SELECT TRUE AS [CREATE RANK], ''same'' AS [RANK], [EventID] & ''_End''   AS [ITEM] FROM [timeline$] 
   WHERE [EndYear] = {ID} AND  [StartYear] & [StartQuarter] <> [EndYear] & [EndQuarter]
  '
  AS [SQL FOR DATA]
Apply styling to the event nodes

SELECT [EventID] & '_Start'                AS [Item], 
       [StartYear] & '\n' & [StartQuarter] AS [Label], 
       'Start'                             AS [Style Name] 
FROM   [timeline$]
WHERE  [StartYear] & [StartQuarter] <> [EndYear] & [EndQuarter]

SELECT [EventID] & '_End'                AS [Item], 
       [EndYear] & '\n' & [EndQuarter]   AS [Label], 
       'Finish'                          AS [Style Name] 
FROM   [timeline$] 
WHERE  [StartYear] & [StartQuarter] <> [EndYear] & [EndQuarter]

SELECT [EventID] & '_Start'                AS [Item], 
       [StartYear] & '\n' & [StartQuarter] AS [Label],  
       'Same'                              AS [Style Name] 
FROM   [timeline$]
WHERE  [StartYear] & [StartQuarter] = [EndYear] & [EndQuarter]

Clear the 'data' worksheet

LOG ENVIRONMENT
Specify the workbook containing the data
SET DATA FILE
Create the edges

SELECT [From Column] AS [Item], 
       [To Column]   AS [Related Item] 
FROM   [Worksheet Name$]
Create the nodes

SELECT [Node Id Column]    AS [Item],
       [Node Label Column] AS [Label],
       [Node Style Column] AS [Style Name]
FROM   [Worksheet Name$] 
WHERE  ...
Create edges which chain a set of nodes

SELECT [Node Id Column] AS [ITEM], 
       TRUE             AS [CREATE EDGES]
FROM   [Worksheet Name$]
WHERE  ...
Create a subgraph, with constraints set to rank specified as either 'same' | 'min' | 'source' | 'max' | 'sink'.

Rank constraints on the nodes in a subgraph. If rank="same", all nodes are placed on the same rank. If rank="min", all nodes are placed on the minimum rank. If rank="source", all nodes are placed on the minimum rank, and the only nodes on the minimum rank belong to some subgraph whose rank attribute is "source" or "min". Analogous criteria hold for rank="max" and rank="sink". (Note: the minimum rank is topmost or leftmost, and the maximum rank is bottommost or rightmost.)

SELECT [Node Id Column] AS [ITEM], 
       TRUE             AS [CREATE RANK],
       'same'           AS [RANK]
FROM   [Worksheet Name$]
WHERE  ...
Split text for labels at first blank after 10 characters

SELECT [Label Column] AS [Label],
       10             AS [SPLIT LENGTH],
       ...
Specify the line ending (\l, \n, \r, | etc.) to use when splitting a label

SELECT [Label Column] AS [Label],
       10             AS [SPLIT LENGTH],
       '\r'           AS [LINE ENDING],
       ...
Group nodes into a cluster

SELECT [Cluster Id Column]         AS [CLUSTER],
       [Cluster Label Column]      AS [CLUSTER LABEL],
       [Cluster Style Name Column] AS [CLUSTER STYLE NAME],
       [Cluster Attributes]        AS [CLUSTER ATTRIBUTES],
       [Cluster Tooltip Column]    AS [CLUSTER TOOLTIP],
       [Node Id Column]            AS [Item],
       [Node Label Column]         AS [Label],
       [Node Style Name Column]    AS [Style Name],
       ...
Group nodes into two level clusters

SELECT [Outer Cluster Id Column]         AS [CLUSTER],
       [Outer Cluster Label Column]      AS [CLUSTER LABEL],
       [Outer Cluster Style Name Column] AS [CLUSTER STYLE NAME],
       [Outer Cluster Attributes]        AS [CLUSTER ATTRIBUTES],
       [Outer Cluster Tooltip Column]    AS [CLUSTER TOOLTIP],

       [Inner Cluster Id Column]         AS [SUBCLUSTER],
       [Inner Cluster Label Column]      AS [SUBCLUSTER LABEL],
       [Inner Cluster Style Name Column] AS [SUBCLUSTER STYLE NAME],
       [Inner Cluster Attributes]        AS [SUBCLUSTER ATTRIBUTES],
       [Inner Cluster Tooltip Column]    AS [SUBCLUSTER TOOLTIP],

       [Node Id Column]                  AS [Item],
       [Node Label Column]               AS [Label],
       [Node Style Name Column]          AS [Style Name],
       ...

Loop count substitution strings (useful in sortv= attributes, style names, and labels). 
  %clc% = Cluster count
  %scc% = Subcluster count
  %rsc% = Record set count

SELECT 'sortv=%clc%'    AS [CLUSTER ATTRIBUTES],
       'Border %clc% '  AS [CLUSTER STYLE NAME],
       'sortv=%scc%'    AS [SUBCLUSTER ATTRIBUTES],
       'sortv=%rsc%'    AS [Attributes],
       ...
FROM   [Worksheet Name$] 
WHERE  ...
ORDER BY [Outer Cluster Label Column] ASC,
         [Inner Cluster Label Column] ASC,
         [Node Label Column]          ASC
Show the graph immediately after all SQL statements processed
PREVIEW [ AS ( DIRECTED | UNDIRECTED ) GRAPH ]
Publish graphs as files
PUBLISH [ ALL VIEWS ] [ AS ( DIRECTED | UNDIRECTED ) GRAPH ] [ file prefix ]

buttons.screenTip: Describes the attributes used by various Graphviz tools
buttons.superTip: The table gives the name of the attribute, the graph components (node, edge, etc.) which use the attribute and the type of the attribute (strings representing legal values of that type). Where applicable, the table also gives a default value for the attribute, a minimum allowed setting for numeric attributes, and certain restrictions on the use of the attribute.
